title: Quota & Rate-Limit Audit Traceability Framework
creator: Priya Desai
description:
Goal: design and implement an auditable, tamper-evident traceability framework for quota checks, rate-limit enforcement, quota updates, and billing-facing usage records. This ticket covers the logging schema, retention tiers, access controls, reconciliation jobs, test harnesses, and SOC2 evidence artifacts.

Scope:
- Instrument rate-limit and quota evaluation code paths (API edge, internal gateways, worker/async billing pipeline) to emit a single canonical audit event per logical action (quota_check, rate_limit_enforce, quota_topup, quota_adjustment, override, billing_charge, billing_reconcile).
- Define minimal event fields required for audits: event_id, timestamp(UTC ISO8601), request_id, customer_id/org_id, route/model, policy_id, quota_bucket, allowance_before, allowance_after, tokens_consumed, enforcement_result, actor (service|user|admin), reason_code, linked_charge_id, hashed_payload (for integrity), service_version, region, ingestion_shard.
- Establish retention tiers: hot (90 days, immediate access), warm (up to 2 years, queryable archive), cold (up to 3 years, S3 glacier/long-term) to satisfy billing and regulatory evidence requirements.
- Log integrity: events signed by service HMAC at write-time and appended to an append-only ledger (object-versioning + HMAC chain) to produce tamper-evidence for auditors.
- Access controls: RBAC for logs with separation of duties (billing_read, billing_admin, compliance_admin), enforced at the storage and SIEM query layers. All access must be logged (audit-of-audit).
- Reconciliation: daily and weekly batch jobs that reconcile billing charges to usage events with discrepancy reports and automated alerts if discrepancy rate > 0.05% or if any org shows > $100 of unallocated charges. Reconciliation artifacts archived for auditors.
- Evidence & playbooks: produce SOC2-friendly artifacts (log retention policy doc, data mapping, sample reconciliation reports, list of roles and privileges, PRs and deployment timeline).
- Integrations: forward canonical events to Splunk/Datadog and ingest to a dedicated billing analytics warehouse (Snowflake) with denormalized tables for fast queries.

Trade-offs / decisions:
- Chosen approach is to emit canonical events at the API edge rather than retrofitting later pipeline steps — ensures single source of truth for enforcement events but requires careful batching to avoid latency impact.
- Use HMAC-chain ledger + object storage versioning rather than full blockchain — reasonable tamper-evidence with lower operational complexity.
- Retention choices set to 3 years to balance auditor expectations and storage cost; team can compress/pseudonymize fields for cold storage.

Deliverables:
1) JSON schema (Avro/Protobuf) for the canonical audit event and example producers/consumers.
2) Instrumentation PRs for API gateway and billing workers (links below).
3) Reconciliation job (airflow DAG + unit/integration tests) and monthly reconciliation report template.
4) Security and access-control matrix + Table of evidence for SOC2 readiness.
5) Test plan and QA checklist (synthetic replay + chaos tests to validate lossless capture under burst).

Success criteria:
- End-to-end tests show 1:1 mapping between enforcement events and stored audit events for 99.99% of sampled requests under normal traffic.
- Reconciliation job can detect and explain >95% of discrepancies.
- SOC2 reviewer can validate retention, access-control, and log-integrity artifacts during audit window.
comments: 2025-02-20 Priya Desai: Initial ticket created after compliance sync. Outlined scope and high-level decisions. Asked infra and security for input on HMAC ledger feasibility.

2025-02-24 Martin Hsu: Spike complete for ledger prototype (github.com/redwood/infra/pulls/5432). Prototype signs events and stores batches with versioned S3 objects. Observed ~1.8ms median extra latency on edge path when batching at 50ms windows. Will iterate to reduce latency.

2025-02-28 Security Review (Ana Vega): Reviewed access-control matrix and suggested mandatory separation of duties; requested that key rotation policy be documented and KMS envelope encryption be used for HMAC keys.

2025-03-01 PM Review (Liam O'Connor): Confirmed SOC2 evidence requirements and requested inclusion of sample reconciliation artifacts and auditor-facing README in Confluence (https://confluence.redwood/billing/quota-audit-framework).

2025-03-03 Eng Design Review: Decided to emit canonical events at API edge to avoid downstream inference loss. Agreed on epoched batching (max 50ms) and async flush to ledger to balance latency and throughput.
2025-03-05 Martin Hsu: Added reconciliation job outline and test cases. Created draft PR for schema (github.com/redwood/platform/pulls/5478). Next: integration tests and security sign-off.
